overall_summary: Data sample is small, but family and relationship dynamics clearly outperform general philosophical or motivational shorts. The video about wives/husbands achieved a major outlier view count (1655 views), while family-centric content consistently pulls moderate engagement.

winning_patterns.pattern: Core family and marital relationship dynamics
winning_patterns.evidence: Wife/husband emotional video (or5gtaBpRVY) gained 1655 views; mother and father shorts (OfHrAp3r1G8, v8krtdmxbPs) performed steadily better than generic sister/brother variants.
winning_patterns.action: Focus heavily on husband-wife and parent-child emotional friction and unspoken sacrifices.

winning_patterns.pattern: Direct question or conversational hooks addressing a specific person
winning_patterns.evidence: Titles like 'माँ जब पूछती है...' and 'पत्नी की ये बात...' generated the highest views and like counts.
winning_patterns.action: Use specific second-person or situational relational hooks in the titles.

weak_patterns.evidence: First sister video got 18 views (jfmMztnam_A), and re-uploading or repeating the exact theme yielded low returns (130 views on fAAoIQCRMXU).
weak_patterns.action: Avoid immediate duplicate themes within the same week; diversify across relationship types.

weak_patterns.evidence: Self-motivation/life lessons like 'तुम थके हो… हारे नहीं' underperformed compared to specific relationship observations.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid pure motivation; anchor every script in interpersonal relationships and emotional reality.

next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the winning husband-wife emotional dynamic pattern seen in the top-performing video while addressing deep-rooted relationship realities.

experiment: Testing if husband-wife relationship nuance can repeat the outlier success of the previous top-performing video or if it was a one-off anomaly.
